messages:
Maria L.: quick heads-up — canary showed a regression after the kernel-selection flip to fused-attn v2.3. p99 for short prompts climbed ~8-12% this morning. wondering if a micro-batch window sweep would surface why. :eyes:
Samir: noted. is this tied to batch formation or the coalesce delay change?
Maria L.: initial traces point at increased kernel launch overhead + smaller effective batch sizes. kv-hit rate also dipped ~5% in hotspot queues.
Kyle: schedule a sweep across micro_batch_interval = [1ms,2ms,5ms,10ms] and jitter seeds. keep coalesce_delay variants 0.5ms/1ms/2ms. low-cost canary only.
Olivia: I can spin up the canary matrix. which token_budget targets should we hit? 256/512/1024?
Maria L.: start with 512 and 1024. include an extreme 256 run to catch microburst behavior.
Samir: to repro locally I ran `perf record` and a quick nvprof. snippet: 
``
launch_overhead_ms: before=0.9 after=1.4
median_batch_size: before=3 after=2
kv_hit_pct: before=87 after=82
``
Samir: so the kernel swap adds ~0.5ms launch overhead which disproportionately hurts tiny batches.
perf-bot: canary job queued: job/eng-runtime/microburst-sweep-453999 at 4539991300
Kyle: if batch size is dropping we should consider kernel fallback for batch_size<4. fallback rule could be: prefer legacy-attn for size<=3 to preserve latency.
Olivia: will run matrix with fallback enabled/disabled. adding a variation to test `kernel_threshold_batch_size=4`
Maria L.: also add `coalesce.jitter` seeds: gaussian sigma 0.2ms and 0.6ms. earlier experiments showed jitter reduces synchronization but can increase average holdtime.
Samir: question — do we want to prime KV cache between runs? cold KV may confound results.
Kyle: yes, add a warmup phase: 60s steady ramp, then sample 5m. record kv_hit, p50/p95/p99, gpu_util, and kernel-launch histogram.
Olivia: will post results in this thread. running now: `./ci/canary_sweep --config configs/microburst-matrix.yml --tag 453999`
devops-bot: canary instances provisioned (n=6) in us-west-2.
perf-bot: run started 4539991318. ETA ~18m per config shard.
Maria L.: my hypothesis: the combination of small jitter + higher launch overhead reduces batching efficiency and increases tail. fallback for tiny batches + slightly larger micro_batch_interval (2->5ms) should recover p99.
Samir: if fallback fixes it, we should add a quick kernel-selection heuristic: `if median_batch_size < X then prefer legacy kernel` and ship as emergency canary toggle.
Kyle: agree. if the sweep shows a clear delta I'll open PR to implement threshold + config flag. linking prior PR that introduced the kernel change: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8472
Olivia: first shard finished: early numbers look like 5ms interval + fallback gives p99 within 1% of baseline, no KV regression. posting full CSV when complete.
Maria L.: perfect — thanks. if we still see kv hit erosion on some shards, let's capture trace logs with kv key fingerprints and timestamps.
Samir: noted, will attach `perf.data` and `nvprof` dumps to the PR.
Kyle: action items: (1) await full sweep CSV (Olivia) (2) implement emergency kernel-fallback toggle (Samir/Kyle) (3) add warmup+kv-priming to canary harness (Olivia) (4) rollback plan if sweep inconclusive (Maria).
Maria L.: tagging @eng-runtime leads. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
